privacy-policy.title: Privacy Policy
sections: 1. Introduction

ABF Accounting Services Ltd explains how it collects, uses, shares, stores and protects personal data when people use the website or engage accounting, tax, payroll, bookkeeping, company-formation or related services. The policy operates alongside engagement terms and service-specific notices.
2. Key Definitions

Personal data is information relating to an identified or identifiable person. ABF acts as data controller where it decides why and how personal data is processed; suppliers may act as processors when they handle information on ABF’s instructions. Processing includes collection, use, storage, disclosure, alteration and deletion.
3. About ABF Accounting Services Ltd

ABF Accounting Services Ltd is a private company registered in England and Wales providing accounting, tax, payroll, bookkeeping, company-formation and related business support. The current website lists the registered office as 18 Thricknells Close, Luton, LU3 3RP.
4. Scope of This Policy

The policy covers personal data collected through the ABF website, email, telephone, forms, meetings and professional-service delivery. Third-party websites or platforms linked from ABF may apply their own privacy terms and should be reviewed separately.
5. Our Data Protection Principles

ABF’s handling of personal data is based on lawfulness, fairness and transparency; purpose limitation; data minimisation; accuracy; storage limitation; integrity, confidentiality and accountability. Information should only be kept for a defined purpose and for no longer than reasonably required.
6. Types of Personal Data We Collect

Depending on the service, ABF may process contact details, company and director information, billing details, financial and tax records, correspondence, identity documents and information supplied during onboarding. Website use can also generate technical data such as IP address, browser, device and analytics information.
7. Legal Basis for Processing Personal Data

Processing may be necessary to perform a contract, meet legal or regulatory duties, pursue legitimate interests, or act on valid consent where consent is the appropriate basis. The lawful basis depends on the purpose and the nature of the information involved.
8. How We Use Your Personal Data

ABF may use personal data to deliver accounting and tax services, prepare filings, register companies, maintain records, answer enquiries, communicate service updates, meet regulatory obligations and improve operations. Marketing should only be sent where the applicable legal basis and user preferences allow.
9. Sharing Your Personal Data

Information may be shared with HMRC, Companies House, professional advisers, secure technology providers, payment or banking providers, identity-verification services and suppliers needed to deliver the agreed service. Sharing should be limited to what is necessary and supported by suitable confidentiality and data-protection controls.
10. International Transfers

ABF does not routinely need to transfer data outside the UK or EEA. Where a provider causes an international transfer, appropriate safeguards should be used, such as an adequacy arrangement, recognised contractual safeguards and suitable processing terms.
11. Data Retention

Retention depends on tax, accounting, AML, contractual and legal requirements. The current ABF policy refers to six years for certain financial records and five years after the business relationship for AML documentation, while marketing preferences are generally retained until a person opts out or the record is no longer needed.
12. Data Security

ABF states that it uses measures such as access controls, password protection, encrypted storage, supplier controls, monitoring and staff training. If a personal-data breach occurs, the impact should be assessed and affected individuals or regulators notified where required by law.
13. Your Rights

Depending on the circumstances, individuals may have rights to be informed, access data, correct inaccuracies, request deletion, restrict processing, receive certain data in a portable format, object to processing and challenge certain automated decisions. Requests can be made using ABF’s published contact details.
14. Cookies and Analytics

The website may use cookies and similar technologies for essential operation, user preferences and analytics. Non-essential technologies should be managed in line with applicable consent requirements, with more detail provided in the Cookie Policy.
15. Contact Us

Privacy questions and rights requests can be sent to support@abfaccounting.com or through ABF’s published telephone details. Requests should contain enough information for ABF to identify the person and understand what right is being exercised.
16. Complaints
Individuals can raise concerns directly with ABF and can also complain to the Information Commissioner’s Office if they believe their data-protection rights have not been handled appropriately.
17. Policy Updates

ABF may update the policy when law, technology, services or internal processes change. The website should display the latest approved version and an updated date so visitors can identify the current policy.

terms-and-conditions-of-engagement.title: Terms & Conditions of Engagement
sections: 1. Definitions

These terms define ABF Accounting Services Ltd, the client, the agreement, the services and the engagement letter. The engagement letter or proposal sets the client-specific scope while these general terms provide the wider contractual framework for the professional relationship.
2. Commencement and Acceptance

The engagement begins when the client accepts the engagement letter, proposal or otherwise proceeds with the agreed services. Material changes to scope, fees or responsibilities should be recorded in writing so both parties have a clear and current record of the agreement.
3. Scope of Services

ABF may provide annual accounts, Corporation Tax, Self Assessment, VAT, payroll, CIS, bookkeeping, business-start-up support, contractor services, registered-office support and other professional work. The exact deliverables for an individual client are those stated in the applicable engagement letter or proposal.
4. Our Responsibilities

ABF agrees to carry out the agreed work with reasonable skill and care and in accordance with relevant UK law and applicable accounting requirements. Where authorised, ABF may contact a previous accountant for records and may quote separately for reconstruction work if information is unavailable or incomplete.
5. Your Responsibilities

Clients must provide complete and accurate records on time, disclose relevant transactions and liabilities, review and approve drafts where required, remain aware of statutory responsibilities and notify ABF about material changes to the business, ownership, address, employees or contact details.
6. Fees, Billing and Payment

Fees may be fixed, monthly, hourly or transaction-based depending on the engagement. Invoices are payable using the agreed method and within the stated period. Fees may be reviewed where costs increase or where the client’s size, complexity or required scope changes materially. Work outside the agreed scope can require a separate quotation.
7. Cancellations and Refunds

Cancellation or refund rights depend on the service, the work already completed and the contractual terms accepted by the client. Where notice, administrative charges or minimum service periods apply, those requirements should be retained exactly in the approved engagement documentation.
8. Late Payments and Debt Recovery

Overdue fees can affect ABF’s ability to continue work. The approved terms may allow interest, suspension of services or recovery action where invoices remain unpaid. Any director or personal-liability provision should be retained exactly where it legally applies.
9. Confidentiality and Data Protection

Information received from the client should be kept confidential except where disclosure is authorised or required by law, regulation or a competent authority. ABF processes personal data under UK data-protection law and may use secure cloud systems and approved service providers to deliver the engagement.
10. Compliance, Authorisation and AML

Clients must provide information needed for identity verification and anti-money-laundering checks and should supply HMRC authorisation codes promptly where ABF is to act as agent. ABF may decline, suspend or end an engagement where legal or regulatory compliance requirements cannot be satisfied.
11. Communication and Recordkeeping

ABF may communicate through email, telephone, client portals and other agreed channels. Records can be retained for the period required by law, regulation, insurance or professional obligations. Where appropriate and authorised, documents can be transferred securely to a successor adviser.
12. Service-Specific Provisions

Service-specific requirements apply to work such as VAT, payroll, bookkeeping and contractor support. VAT clients must provide complete records and approve returns before submission; payroll clients must provide accurate starter, leaver, pay, tax-code and statutory-leave information in time for RTI reporting. Complex or specialist matters fall outside standard scope unless specifically agreed.
13. Registered Office Address (If Applicable)

Where registered-office services are included, the service should be limited to the statutory-mail and address scope stated in the engagement. Clients remain responsible for maintaining accurate company information and for responding promptly to official correspondence forwarded by ABF.
14. Referrals and Promotions

ABF may recommend third-party services and may receive referral or commission income where permitted. Promotions can be subject to qualifying conditions, minimum service periods and exclusions for third-party software, regulatory fees or other external charges.
15. Termination of Services

Either party may terminate in accordance with the notice period stated in the approved terms. On termination, outstanding fees become due and ABF should reasonably cooperate with an authorised handover to a new adviser, subject to legal, regulatory and payment requirements.
16. Liability and Indemnity

The approved terms limit ABF’s liability for claims connected with the relevant service and exclude certain indirect or consequential losses where legally permitted. Clients remain responsible for losses caused by incorrect, incomplete or late information or by failing to act on agreed advice.
17. Insurance
ABF states that it maintains professional indemnity insurance appropriate to its work. Evidence of cover may be made available where required and subject to the terms and limits of the policy.
18. Governing Law and Jurisdiction
The engagement is governed by the laws of England and Wales. Disputes relating to the agreement are subject to the jurisdiction stated in the approved contractual terms.
19. Variation and Updates

ABF may update its standard engagement terms from time to time. Material changes affecting an existing client relationship should be communicated appropriately, while the website should display the most recent approved general terms.

terms-and-conditions-for-one-off-service.title: Terms & Conditions for One-Off Services
sections: 1. Introduction

These terms apply when a client buys a one-off accounting or tax service from ABF Accounting Services Ltd, whether through the website or by direct agreement. One-off services are transactional rather than an ongoing advisory engagement, so the client should confirm the service is suitable before purchase.
2. Scope of One-Off Services

The service includes only the deliverables described at the point of purchase or in ABF’s written confirmation. One-off work can include defined accounting, tax or filing tasks; additional or more complex work falls outside scope unless separately agreed. Some packages may involve trusted third parties where this is disclosed and necessary to fulfil the service.
3. Client Obligations

Clients must provide complete, accurate and timely records, respond to reasonable information requests and review drafts or filings that require approval. Delays, penalties or additional costs caused by late, incomplete or inaccurate client information remain the client’s responsibility.
4. Service Delivery and Timeframes

ABF recommends engaging well before statutory deadlines so there is time to obtain records, complete the work and secure approval. Late engagements may attract additional charges, may be refused, or may not be guaranteed before the deadline. The current terms specifically warn about late Self Assessment engagements close to 31 January.
5. Fees, Payments, and Refund Policy

Full payment is normally required before work starts and the quoted fee applies to the specified scope. The current terms state that one-off purchases are generally non-refundable after purchase unless ABF is unable to deliver for reasons within its control. Unused services or missed deadlines caused by the client may result in the fee being forfeited.
6. Limitations of Liability

ABF is not responsible for penalties, interest or losses caused by inaccurate, incomplete or late information supplied by the client, or by events outside ABF’s reasonable control. The current one-off terms cap liability to the fee paid for the specific service, subject to any legal rights that cannot be excluded.
7. Confidentiality and Data Protection

Client information is handled confidentially and in line with the Privacy Policy and applicable data-protection law. Where an approved external partner is involved in delivery, only information reasonably needed to provide that part of the service should be shared.
8. Governing Law and Jurisdiction

These terms are governed by the laws of England and Wales. Disputes arising from the one-off service are subject to the jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales, subject to any rights that cannot legally be excluded.
9. Changes to Terms

ABF may update the published terms from time to time to reflect service, legal or operational changes. The latest approved version should be available on the website and should apply in accordance with the effective date stated in that version.
10. Contact Us

Questions about a one-off service can be directed to support@abfaccounting.com or ABF’s published telephone number before purchase, particularly where the client is unsure whether the selected service is appropriate for their circumstances.

cookie-policy.title: Cookie Policy
sections: Approved Cookie Policy content

This Cookie Policy explains how ABF Accounting Services Ltd may use cookies and similar storage or access technologies on its website. It should be read together with the Privacy Policy, which explains how personal data is handled more broadly and how individuals can exercise their data-protection rights.
Current cookie-policy introduction

Cookies are small files or identifiers stored on or accessed from a user’s device. Similar technologies can include local storage, tracking pixels, scripts, tags and other methods that remember information, support website functions or measure how people use an online service. Some technologies may be strictly necessary for security, session management, forms or remembering a privacy choice.
Cookie categories and purposes

ABF may use different categories of technologies for essential operation, preferences, functionality and analytics. Non-essential analytics or performance technologies should only operate in accordance with the applicable consent rules. The final production policy should maintain a current inventory showing the technology name, provider, purpose, category and duration where relevant.
Consent and preference controls

Where consent is required, users should receive clear information before non-essential technologies are used and should be able to make an active choice. Rejecting non-essential technologies should be straightforward, and consent should not be inferred merely from continued browsing. Visitors should also be able to revisit or withdraw their choices through the site’s privacy or cookie settings.
Third-party / analytics information

Embedded tools, analytics services, social features, maps, video, payment services or other external platforms may place or access their own technologies when used. The final live policy should identify any relevant third parties and link to their privacy or cookie information where appropriate. Where these technologies process personal data, the Privacy Policy and UK data-protection requirements also apply.
Retention and updates

Cookie and storage-access information should be reviewed whenever ABF adds or removes technologies, changes providers, changes analytics or advertising configuration, or when relevant law or regulatory guidance changes. Browser controls can also block, delete or restrict cookies, although disabling some technologies may affect website functions.
Contact information

Questions about cookies, privacy settings or how ABF uses website data can be directed to support@abfaccounting.com or the other contact details published on the ABF website. The implemented site should provide a simple route for users to change non-essential cookie preferences at any time.

modern-slavery-statement.title: Modern Slavery Statement
sections: 1. Introduction

ABF’s statement explains the steps the organisation takes to reduce the risk of modern slavery and human trafficking in its operations and supply chain. The current statement is presented as a section 54 transparency statement and was approved on 1 September 2024.
2. Business Description

ABF describes itself as a payroll and accounting outsourcing business. Relevant risks may arise through employment practices, outsourced service arrangements, vendors, technology suppliers and other third parties used to support operations.
3. Core Values and Governance

ABF describes values centred on listening, simplicity and doing things correctly. Governance responsibilities include maintaining appropriate controls, reviewing conflicts of interest and ensuring management oversight of ethical and supplier-related risks.
4. Supply Chains

The current statement refers to assessment of new suppliers and outsourcing providers, anti-slavery expectations in supplier agreements, a risk-based review process and due diligence under a Supplier & Outsourcing Policy. Higher-risk relationships should receive proportionate additional review and oversight.
5. People

ABF aims to maintain fair, inclusive and transparent employment practices. Controls can include eligibility and background checks where appropriate, clear employment terms, staff policies, engagement surveys and confidential routes for employees to raise concerns without retaliation.
6. Customers and Partners

ABF also applies due diligence to customers and business partners. Where relevant, partner onboarding may include asking for evidence of policies, statements or controls that demonstrate a comparable commitment to preventing forced labour and trafficking.
7. Training

Staff should receive modern-slavery awareness training, with additional training for people involved in supplier management, recruitment, compliance or risk. Refresher training helps keep warning signs, escalation routes and organisational expectations visible.
8. Compliance

The statement refers to internal and external audit activity supporting compliance with relevant policies and procedures. Monitoring should consider both the effectiveness of controls and whether risks have changed as suppliers, markets or operating arrangements evolve.
9. Test of Adequacy

The current statement records zero reports indicating modern-slavery practices within the organisation at the time of publication. The absence of reports should not replace ongoing monitoring, staff awareness or appropriate investigation of future concerns.
10. Policies

The statement references a Modern Slavery Policy, Supplier and Outsourcing Policy, Staff Handbook and Code of Conduct, Recruitment Policy and Whistleblowing Policy. Together these documents support prevention, due diligence, reporting and response.
11. Moving Forward

ABF commits to reviewing the statement and related procedures regularly, improving staff awareness and monitoring modern-slavery issues through governance channels. Future statements should summarise progress, material risks identified and actions taken during the reporting period. The approved website version should retain the appropriate signatory and approval date.
